root_cause: No execution feedback: unverified literals/joins silently yield empty results
what: solve.py now executes the draft query, and if it errors or returns 0 rows it probes actual sample values of the string columns used in the draft and asks the policy for one corrected query (second allowed call). system_prompt.md adds concise rules on exact stored literals, NULL-safe NOT IN, and returning full entity rows when the question names an entity without specific attributes.
decision: s1 delivers a large measured gain (83.33 -> 90.0) with only one regression, and its mechanism—execute the draft, probe actual stored literals on error/empty results, then allow one grounded repair—is a general text-to-SQL pattern rather than task-specific patching; the token increase is justified by the score jump and stays within the admissibility cost rule.

what: Add DISTINCT-for-join-duplicates and select-all-columns-of-joined-tables guidance to the system prompt, and extend solve.py's repair trigger to fire when a multi-table query returns repeated rows (with targeted feedback suggesting DISTINCT / deduplicated join path). This targets sp0536/sp0600 duplicates deterministically and nudges sp0755 toward full-entity projection.

root_cause: Repair only triggers on empty/error results, so successfully-executing queries with join fan-out duplicates or too-narrow projections are never checked
what: solve.py now also triggers the second policy call when the executed draft returns duplicate result rows, and supplies evidence-based alternatives (an executed SELECT DISTINCT variant, plus an executed full-entity-row variant when the draft projects a narrow column subset) for the policy to choose from; system_prompt.md gains one general rule about DISTINCT under one-to-many joins. This targets duplicate-row and projection-shape failures that the empty-result-only feedback silently passes.

root_cause: Join fan-out emits duplicate rows and entity questions get narrow projections; repair only fires on empty/error results so these silent shape errors survive
what: Extend the existing second-call repair to also fire when an executed multi-table draft returns repeated result rows: it probes stored values, executes a SELECT DISTINCT variant (and, for 'which/show/list <entity>' questions, an executed T.* variant of the first table) and shows both real results so the policy picks the right dedup/projection. Also tighten two prompt rules: default to DISTINCT after joins that can multiply rows unless multiplicity is asked for, and return all columns of every joined base table for entity questions.
